explorer.tabLabel: PropertyMay help cover sanctuaries, fellowship halls, offices, kitchens, and con
explorer.tabDesc: May help cover sanctuaries, fellowship halls, offices, kitchens, and contents including audio-visual equipment against covered direct physical loss — subject to policy causes of loss, limits, deductibles, and valuation.
explorer.detailTitle: Stained glass and AV can exceed ordinary contents limits
explorer.detailDescription: Houses of worship often hold specialty property — stained glass, organs, historic finishes, and production-grade AV — that may need agreed values or scheduling beyond generic contents limits. Heritage buildings may have restoration requirements that differ from standard replacement-cost assumptions. Kitchens, community halls, and office wings add property values separate from the sanctuary itself. Confirm what your organization owns versus what a landlord or denomination carries on a master policy.

explorer.tabLabel: LiabilityMay help respond to certain third-party bodily injury or property-damag
explorer.tabDesc: May help respond to certain third-party bodily injury or property-damage claims arising from visitor incidents on premises, parking areas, and congregational activities — subject to policy terms, exclusions, and limits.
explorer.detailTitle: A winter parking-lot fall reaches the organization
explorer.detailDescription: Congregation and visitor exposure includes services, fellowship events, food preparation in church kitchens, and parking-lot injuries — especially in winter. Hall rentals to third parties may create premises exposure and certificate requirements; renters often need their own event liability depending on the contract. Off-site mission trips and community programs may extend beyond the primary address depending on policy wording and what was disclosed during underwriting — not every activity is automatically covered.

explorer.tabLabel: CounsellingWhere included in the program, may help address certain claims arisin
explorer.tabDesc: Where included in the program, may help address certain claims arising from pastoral or spiritual counselling services — subject to policy definitions, qualifications, credentials, and exclusions. Distinct from general premises liability.
explorer.detailTitle: Counselling allegations need the right policy part
explorer.detailDescription: Pastoral counselling, spiritual direction, and marriage support offered by clergy or lay counsellors may create professional liability exposure separate from a slip in the nave. Whether coverage responds depends on policy wording, counsellor credentials, and whether services were disclosed during underwriting. Licensed mental-health practitioners may need different professional coverage than informal pastoral care — disclose all counselling programs to your broker.

explorer.tabLabel: AbuseWhere available as a specialized coverage, may help address certain claims
explorer.tabDesc: Where available as a specialized coverage, may help address certain claims alleging abuse or misconduct involving youth or vulnerable persons — subject to policy wording, limits, exclusions, and underwriting review. Not automatic on general liability.
explorer.detailTitle: Youth ministry deserves its own coverage review
explorer.detailDescription: Youth ministries, childcare rooms, and programs serving vulnerable persons may need abuse or molestation liability reviewed separately — many general liability forms contain abuse exclusions. Specialized coverage, where offered, is policy-dependent and may review screening, supervision, and safeguarding policies. Coverage may address organizational response to allegations subject to wording — not indemnification of intentional criminal conduct by a perpetrator. Safeguarding practices support safer programs but do not replace appropriate coverage review.
